p3.text: Clare's grandfather has got a small __(0)__ near a river. Last week, Clare was in the __(1)__ with her grandmother when she saw something grey and very small. It was a little __(2)__! It ran __(3)__ under the table with some __(4)__ in its mouth. Clare's grandmother wasn't __(5)__ of it. 'That's Pip,' she said. 'He lives in the wall and he helps me: he eats all the old bread.'

p4.title: Cows
p4.text: Cows are big animals __(0)__ live on farms in every country. They eat grass and they drink a lot of water. Farmers get milk __(1)__ their cows in the morning and in the afternoon. We make butter and cheese __(2)__ this milk. A baby cow can walk __(3)__ it is very young, and it goes with its mother. Cows are quiet animals and they __(4)__ got very good ears, so they know you are there before they __(5)__ you.

parts.text: Every year, Daisy goes to her uncle's farm in the countryside. She loves the animals, but her favourite is a small white duck. The duck goes with Daisy all day, and Daisy calls her Snowy.

examples.s: Her favourite animal is a small white ___.

parts.text: One morning, Daisy couldn't find Snowy. She looked in the field, next to the river and behind the tractor, but the duck wasn't there. Then Daisy heard a funny noise in the house. It came from the kitchen.

items.s: Daisy looked next to the ___ and behind the tractor.

parts.text: Snowy was inside one of Uncle Fred's big boots! She slept in it and she didn't want to come out. Now Snowy sleeps in that boot every night, and Uncle Fred wears his old shoes.

p1.scene: Two pictures of the same farm garden. Left: the examiner's picture. Right: your picture.
p1.examiner: Look at the two pictures. Here the cat is on the wall, but here the cat is under the tree. What other differences can you see?
differences: In your picture there are four ducks, but in my picture there are two.
In your picture the horse is brown, but in my picture it is white.
In your picture the bike is behind the house, but in my picture it is next to the door.
In your picture the girl is carrying eggs, but in my picture she is carrying water.
In your picture the tractor is green, but in my picture it is red.

p2.title: The lost sheep
p2.examiner_open: These pictures show a story. It's called 'The lost sheep'. Look at the pictures first. Sam and his grandfather are counting the sheep in the field, and one sheep isn't there. Now you tell the story.
frames: Sam and his grandfather are counting the sheep in the field. One sheep isn't there and they are worried.
Sam and the dog look for the sheep. They walk next to the river and behind the trees.
The dog stops and starts to bark. The sheep is in the water and it can't get out!
Sam and his grandfather help the sheep to come out of the river. The sheep is happy and Sam gives the dog a big dinner.

sets.reason: A tractor isn't an animal. The farmer drives it.
A boot doesn't grow in the ground. You wear it.
A cat doesn't like water. The others do.
A kitchen is inside a house. The others are outside.

p1: Part One. Look at the picture. Listen and look. There is one example.
Grandpa, look at this picture of your farm!
Ha! That's a good one. Who's the girl with the brown cow?
That's Lucy. She's giving grass to it. She isn't afraid of the cows.
Can you see the line? This is an example. Now you listen and draw lines.
And who's the boy on the tractor?
That's me! I'm Sam. I sit on it, but I can't drive it. I'm too young.
You can drive it when you're older.
Who's the woman with the box?
That's my sister Clare. There are eggs in the box. Twelve!
She must walk very slowly, then.
Can you see the man with the black and white dog?
Yes, next to the sheep. Is that your father?
No, that's my uncle Mark. The sheep listen to his dog.
And that girl in the river? What's she doing?
That's Daisy. She's catching a fish. She catches one every afternoon.
And that boy is cleaning the little blue boat.
Fred. We go on the river in that boat when the water is quiet.
Now listen to Part One again.
p2: Part Two. Listen and look. There is one example.
Grandpa, what's the name of your farm?
Green Farm. G-R-E-E-N. Because everything here is green!
Can you see the answer? Now you listen and write.
How many cows have you got?
Thirty-five now. We had thirty last year.
Thirty-five! Have they all got names?
Rocky. R-O-C-K-Y. He works with the sheep.
What time must I get up?
At six. The animals are hungry very early.
Six o'clock! That's early for me.
Your first job is the horses. Give them some water, please.
I give them their food. You give them water.
Yes, you can swim in the river, but you must be with me. It's cold!
Now listen to Part Two again.
p3: Part Three. Listen and look. There is one example.
Sam is telling his teacher about the animals on his grandfather's farm. Where is each animal?
Sam, where are the cows on your grandfather's farm?
They're in the big field all day. They eat and eat.
Can you see the letter A? Now you listen and write a letter in each box.
The horse is under the tree because it's very hot today. It likes the cool grass there.
Yes, five. They're in the river. They swim all day and come back at night.
My cat is on the roof! She goes up when the dog is in the garden.
Next to the tractor. He sleeps there because it's his favourite place.
Have you got mice on the farm?
One! There's a mouse behind the door in the kitchen. My grandmother gives it bread.
Now listen to Part Three again.
p4: Part Four. Look at the pictures. Listen and look. There is one example.
What did Clare see first on the farm?
Clare, what did you see first? A horse?
No, a duck! It was next to the car when we arrived.
We saw them after, in the field.
Can you see the tick? Now you listen and tick the box.
One. Which animal is Mark's favourite?
Do you like the goats, Uncle Mark?
They're funny, but the horses are my favourite. I ride one every morning.
The sheep are the dog's favourite!
Two. What is in the box?
Careful with that box! Are there apples in it?
No, eggs. Twelve eggs from this morning.
The potatoes are in the other box, then.
Three. Where are the children going now?
Are we going to the village this afternoon?
No, first we're going to the river. You can swim there.
No, he's got an old green tractor. He drives it every day.
Five. What did the children have for breakfast?
Did you have cheese for breakfast?
No, we had bread with butter. It was hot and very good.
Now listen to Part Four again.
p5: Part Five. Look at the picture. Listen and look. There is one example.
Here's a picture of a farm garden. Can you see the horse next to the tree?
Can you see the brown horse? This is an example. Now you listen and colour and write.
Now, can you see the cat on the wall?
There's a duck in the water. Can I colour it?
A yellow duck! Like a baby duck.
Can you see the bike behind the house?
Yes. There's a wooden board next to the door with nothing on it. Write the word 'farm'. F-A-R-M.
And now the bird in the tree. Colour it blue, please.
Well done. That's a lovely farm.
Now listen to Part Five again.
